reason: The cited lines show the tool obtains a Puppeteer page/browser and calls `page.select(args.selector, args.value)`. That supplies agent-controlled input (`selector`/`value`) into the current browser page, so it can act as a sink to a webpage that may observe DOM changes/events. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution; launching Puppeteer/Chromium is not itself arbitrary host execution. They also do not show reading or returning non-public data, nor returning attacker-controlled webpage content.
